info.name: Polar AccessLink (aifitnessapi.com)
info.description: Polar AccessLink: OAuth 2.0 and Webhook samples requests built from the vendor documentation aifitnessapi.com quotes. Generated by scripts/build-collections.mjs; no secrets included. https://aifitnessapi.com/collections

item.name: OAuth 2.0
item.description:
Polar AccessLink's authorization-code flow as its documentation describes it, read 2026-11-05. Fill client_id, redirect_uri and scope in an environment of your own and keep client_secret there, never in a shared collection. No refresh request: No refresh flow is documented: the token response lists no refresh_token, and the reference says access tokens do not expire unless revoked.

The same facts, with each source sentence, at https://aifitnessapi.com/integrate/polar-api and https://aifitnessapi.com/tools/oauth-playground.

request.description:
https://flow.polar.com/oauth2/authorization. Authorization endpoint in Polar Flow. Open this URL in a browser (in Postman: copy it from the request bar); the user signs in and Polar AccessLink redirects to {{redirect_uri}} with ?code=… Put that value in the auth_code variable.

Source: Polar AccessLink API v3, “Authentication”, https://www.polar.com/accesslink-api/

Scope: Optional: without it the user is asked to grant every scope linked to your client. Source: Polar AccessLink API v3, “Authentication”, https://www.polar.com/accesslink-api/

Documented scopes (joined with spaces):
- accesslink.read_all: Access to the user's data

PKCE: Not mentioned on the AccessLink reference.

https://polarremote.com/v2/oauth2/token. Token endpoint in Polar Remote, authenticated with HTTP Basic.

Source: Polar AccessLink API v3, “Authentication”, https://www.polar.com/accesslink-api/

Client credentials go as HTTP Basic: {{client_id}} as the user name, {{client_secret}} as the password.

Token lifetime: expires_in is in seconds; Polar's example, 31535999, is about one year. Source: Polar AccessLink API v3, “Authentication”, https://www.polar.com/accesslink-api/

Note: The code expires in 10 minutes and must be used once; reuse is denied and deletes every issued token. Source: Polar AccessLink API v3, “Authentication”, https://www.polar.com/accesslink-api/

Note: redirect_uri goes to the token endpoint only if it was sent to the authorization endpoint. Source: Polar AccessLink API v3, “Authentication”, https://www.polar.com/accesslink-api/

Note: After the exchange, register the user before reading their data. Source: Polar AccessLink API v3, “Authentication”, https://www.polar.com/accesslink-api/

Note: The token request sends Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded and Accept application/json;charset=UTF-8. Source: Polar AccessLink API v3, “Authentication”, https://www.polar.com/accesslink-api/

item.name: Webhook samples
item.description:
Polar AccessLink's documented example notifications, sent to {{local_url}} (your local handler) unchanged. Signature: HMAC-SHA256 of the payload, keyed by the signature_secret_key returned once when you create the webhook, hex, in Polar-Webhook-Signature; the event type is in Polar-Webhook-Event. Source: Polar AccessLink API v3, “Accesslink webhooks” and data models, https://www.polar.com/accesslink-api/

Headers that carry a signature hold the placeholder Polar AccessLink prints, so a handler that verifies signatures will reject these: to send correctly signed requests, use https://aifitnessapi.com/webhooks/send-sample.mjs. Respond: Answer with 200. The PING sent when a webhook is created or its URL changes must get 200 OK, or the change is not made.

Payload library with JSON Schemas: https://aifitnessapi.com/webhooks#polar.
